title: Onboarding takes over twice as long as promised
detail: Promised decision in 3 working days, actual median 7 working days, worst cases past 12.
speaker: Deborah
quote: we promise customers a decision in three working days and we are nowhere near it. Our median is seven working days, and the worst cases go past twelve

title: Large document backlog
detail: 4,200 documents waiting for an analyst, building since about March after volume rose without headcount growth.
speaker: Deborah
quote: Right now we have 4,200 documents waiting for an analyst.

title: Business accounts consume disproportionate analyst time
detail: Business accounts are ~15% of applications but take ~40% of analyst time due to incorporation, directors, PSCs and Companies House checks.
speaker: Deborah
quote: Business accounts. They are only about 15 percent of applications, but they take about 40 percent of my analysts' time.

title: Seasonal peaks roughly double volume
detail: January and September peaks roughly double volumes; January peak risk if not fixed.
speaker: Deborah
quote: January and September are our peaks: volumes roughly double.

title: Manual copy-typing between document viewer and CaseFlow
detail: Analysts copy-type key fields into CaseFlow because CaseFlow cannot read documents; same address typed up to four times in one case, plus constant screen switching.
speaker: Tom
quote: Honestly, the copy-typing. I've typed the same address four times in one case. And switching between the two screens all day.

title: Slow per-document handling time
detail: About six minutes for a clean personal document; twenty minutes or more for a company document.
speaker: Tom
quote: A personal document is about six minutes if it's clean. A company document can be twenty minutes or more, because you're cross-checking directors and owners.

title: Frequent ask-applicant rework
detail: About 31 percent of applications get at least one ask-applicant; returns go to the queue and often a different analyst who starts over, driving backlog.
speaker: Tom
quote: About 31 percent of applications get at least one "ask applicant".

title: Prior OCR pilot failed due to missing confidence signals
detail: A 2024 OCR pilot was abandoned after four months because every field looked equally confident, forcing full rechecking; trust is damaged.
speaker: Tom
quote: We stopped using it after four months. The problem was that it never told you how sure it was. Every field looked equally confident, so we ended up rechecking everything it did, and that was slower than doing it ourselves.

title: Solution must surface confidence and provenance
detail: Analysts will not trust a tool that cannot show where an answer came from or how sure it is.
speaker: Deborah
quote: My analysts will not trust a tool that can't show them where an answer came from.

title: Assistive, not decision-making: human decides every KYC case
detail: Tool may prepare, highlight and suggest, but an analyst decides and is accountable.
speaker: Helen
quote: a person must make every KYC decision. A tool can prepare, highlight and suggest, but an analyst decides and is accountable. That is not negotiable.

title: Full audit trail of decisions and evidence
detail: Must be able to show a regulator who decided what, when, and on what evidence.
speaker: Helen
quote: Whatever the tool does, we must be able to show a regulator who decided what, when, and on what evidence.

title: Point directly to the problematic part of a document
detail: Tom wants the tool to flag which part of a document is the issue so he does not read the whole document.
speaker: Tom
quote: Stop the copy-typing, and show me straight away which part of a document is the problem, so I don't have to read the whole thing to find it.

title: Target of 3 working days before January peak
detail: Success is back inside three working days for most customers before January, with analysts actually wanting to use the tool.
speaker: Deborah
quote: If we're back inside three working days for most customers before the January peak, I'll be happy. And if my analysts actually want to use the tool.

title: Independent model validation required before production
detail: Any model use needs independent model validation; in practice about three weeks, so plan for it.
speaker: Helen
quote: anything that uses a model needs an independent model validation before it goes into production. In practice that takes about three weeks, so plan for it.

title: MLRO sign-off for KYC control changes
detail: Any change to KYC controls needs Helen's sign-off.
speaker: Helen
quote: Any change to our KYC controls needs my sign-off

title: Customer documents must stay in the UK
detail: Processing must stay in AWS London region; no public AI chat tools (already blocked for staff).
speaker: Helen
quote: Customer documents must not leave the UK. Our cloud is AWS in the London region, and nothing goes to public AI chat tools.

title: CaseFlow write access requires vendor change
detail: CaseFlow API is read-only for the team; writing back needs a vendor change, and the last change took eight weeks.
speaker: Tom
quote: CaseFlow has an API, but it's read-only for us. Writing anything back needs a change from the vendor, and the last change took eight weeks.

title: Customer data in history export needs Helen's approval
detail: 18 months of CaseFlow history exists but contains customer data; Helen must agree how an export is handled.
speaker: Deborah
quote: I think so, but it contains customer data, so Helen will need to agree how.

title: How can the 18-month review history be exported given customer data?
detail: Roughly 61,000 document reviews with decisions and reason codes exist; export method and controls to be agreed with Helen.
speaker: Deborah
quote: I think so, but it contains customer data, so Helen will need to agree how.

title: How will CaseFlow integration work given read-only API?
detail: Unresolved how the solution writes results back or avoids copy-typing without a vendor change (last change took eight weeks).
speaker: Tom
quote: CaseFlow has an API, but it's read-only for us.
